description: An RTL structure spec is valid when at least one RTL locale is declared, layout elements have mirroring declarations, navigation has RTL direction reversal, directional icons have RTL variants, left-aligned text has RTL text-align overrides, and all element ids are unique.

rules.description: rtl-spec.json must exist with locales (array) and elements (array). RTL specs without these fields cannot be validated.
The locales array must contain at least one RTL locale string (e.g. ar, he, fa). A spec with no RTL locales has nothing to validate against.
The elements array must contain at least one element. An RTL spec with no elements declares RTL support for nothing.
Every element must declare id, type, and currentDirection (ltr, rtl, or auto). Elements without these fields cannot have their RTL behavior validated.
Every element with type=layout and currentDirection=ltr must declare rtlMirror:true or an rtlOverride object. LTR layouts without mirroring create left-to-right visual flow in RTL locales.
When navigation is declared, it must have rtlReverseDirection:true and rtlBackIcon unless directionNeutral:true. Navigation without RTL reversal shows forward and back icons in the wrong direction.
Every element with type=icon and directional:true must declare rtlVariant. Directional icons like arrows and chevrons show the wrong direction in RTL without a variant.
Every element with type=text and textAlign=left must declare rtlTextAlign as right or start. Hard-coded left alignment pushes RTL text to the wrong side.
All element ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate element ids create ambiguous RTL override references.
